title: Base case for quantified formula evaluation
statement: Let $q$ be a finite Boolean word, let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables, and let $x$ be a finite bit string. If $x$ is the pair encoding of $q$ and the serialization of $\varphi$, $2^{|q|+1}\le B$, and $|x|\le B$, then for every natural number $S<2^{|q|+1}$ there is a run, with all intermediate configurations satisfying the register bound and the machine’s precondition, from the node state with depth $|q|$, assignment stack $S$, and pointer $0$ to the return state carrying the truth value of the quantified formula specification at depth $|q|$ and stack $S$, with pointer $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is the pair encoding of $q$ and the serialization of $\varphi$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, $q$ a finite bit
string, and $\varphi$ a CNF formula over natural-number variables. If $x$ is the pairing
of $q$ with the encoding of $\varphi$, $2^{|q|+1}\le B$, and $|x|\le B$, then the
machine satisfies its run specification at depth $|q|$.
